messages:
incidents-bot: Pager: Unusual KV prefix churn detected on prod-gpu-pool; p95 gen latency > 600ms and node memory > 88%. Escalating to on-call.
oncall-sre: Acknowledged. Spinning up topo and flamegraphs. Initial glance: huge spike in kv.puts for keys under /prefix/ between 02:41-02:44. Continuous-batching queues rising. Marking as active incident.
alice: Was there a deploy around that window? I merged a small template-refactor yesterday evening but nothing scheduled at 02:40.
ben: deploy-bot shows a canary push at 02:39 that included template interpolation change + tokenizer tweak (token merge rule). Could be related.
oncall-sre: Correlating: canary traffic ramped to 10% at 02:38 then steady increase. Put-rate jumped x8 at 02:40. Prefetch hit ratio collapsed.
carla: CS ping: several customers on enterprise plans seeing request timeouts. One reported 500 errors from the generator endpoint starting 02:43.
infra-bot: Running immediate mitigation probe: checking config prefix_cache.enabled and continuous_batching.max_delay.
incidents-bot: Suggest immediate mitigation options: 1) disable prefix cache on affected pool, 2) throttle kv puts, 3) reduce batching window.
oncall-sre: Executing mitigation 1: setting prefix_cache.enabled=false for prod-gpu-pool via infractl. If unsuccessful, fallback to throttles.
infra-bot: Command: infractl clusters update prod-gpu-pool --set prefix_cache.enabled=false -> SUCCESS.
oncall-sre: Observability: mem use plateaued within 90s on hot nodes, but overall latency still elevated due to backlog and timeouts.
ben: Rolling back tokenizer change on canary might be needed but let's see if prefix cache off recovers. I can rollback canary to 0% if necessary.
alice: Log excerpt showing churn pattern (truncated):
```
2025-04-02T02:40:15Z PUT kv/prefix/7f4c9a... size=476
2025-04-02T02:40:15Z PUT kv/prefix/8f4c9a... size=480
2025-04-02T02:40:15Z PUT kv/prefix/9f4c9a... size=468
# suffix differences correspond to minor token split changes
```
oncall-sre: Given that toggle helped, next: throttle kv write rate to mitigate any residual regen storms. Setting kv.put_rate_limit=60/sec/node.
infra-bot: Command: infractl cfg set prod-gpu-pool kv.put_rate_limit 60 -> SUCCESS. Also setting continuous_batching.max_delay_ms=25.
carla: Customer impact summary: 6 customers filed tickets; two enterprise customers (Acct: ENT-91, ENT-77) saw degraded SLAs, one asked for status update.
cs-rep: Noted. CS started outreach to ENT-91 and ENT-77 and provided a short note about degraded performance while we investigate.
oncall-sre: We should prepare a workaround in code: add a pre-hash normalizer for prompt templates to stabilize token boundaries for hashing. But we must be careful: changing hash function can change cache semantics.
ben: Agreed. Alternative: put normalizer behind a feature flag and run 5% canary traffic through it, measure prefix-hit change.
alice: I can draft a minimal normalizer that collapses non-significant whitespace and trims template metadata strings before hashing. Will push to staging.
oncall-sre: In the meantime, set continuous-batching.max_batch_size to 6 to reduce per-call latency; implemented by infra-bot.
infra-bot: Command: infractl cfg set prod-gpu-pool continuous_batching.max_batch_size 6 -> SUCCESS.
alice: Pushed normalizer branch to feature-flagged endpoint. Deploy-bot: starting 5% canary in 03:20 UTC window.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated for feature-flag "prompt_normalizer" on redwood-emi-* models: 5% traffic.
incidents-bot: Taking snapshot for post-incident analysis (logs, kv key dumps, perf traces). Archive link: https://internal/redwood/incidents/2112233445/archive
oncall-sre: Quick check: prefix hit ratio climbed from 3% to 40% after toggle and throttles. Gen latency trending down but still above baseline p95.
carla: CS update: ENT-91 acknowledged the outreach and requested ETA for full fix; they are OK with mitigations but want a timeline.
oncall-sre: Proposed timeline: keep prefix cache disabled until normalizer canary validates for 2 hours; if stable, enable flag-gated normalizer and re-enable prefix cache in controlled fashion.
ben: Rollback plan: if normalizer harms hit rates or causes correctness drift, revert flag and enable prefix cache original hashing. We'll have metric alarms for hit-rate change > -10%.
alice: Canary metrics after 20 min: for the 5% traffic path, prefix key churn reduced by ~85%, cache hit ratio improved, and downstream latency for that cohort is nearly baseline.
oncall-sre: Good sign. Schedule next step: expand canary to 25% at 04:15 UTC, monitor 30m, then 100% and then re-enable prefix cache with cautious ramp.
cs-rep: Notifying affected customers of planned fix window and next update in 45 minutes.
oncall-sre: Handoff: I'll remain as primary until prefix-cache is re-enabled. @alice you own the canary and patch review; @ben you own rollback/tracking alarms; @infra-bot manage config gates.
incidents-bot: Incident severity set to SEV3. Creating postmortem ticket linking snapshot and actions.
oncall-sre: Closing pager for immediate memory crisis. Keeping channel open for canary updates and customer comms. If any metric regresses, re-open immediately.
carla: Thanks team. CS will collect impacted request IDs and coordinate follow-ups.
incidents-bot: Pager closed by oncall-sre at 03:47 UTC. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem owner: alice.
